questions.q: Cartilaginous lesions produce calcifications because they are which cell predominant?
questions.exp: Cartilaginous lesions are chondrocyte predominant, hence they calcify. (Book p129)

questions.q: Popcorn / ring-and-arc (O-ring sign) calcification is seen in:
opts: Giant cell tumor, ABC and SBC
questions.exp: Popcorn/ring-and-arc/O-ring calcification: chondroma, osteochondroma, chondrosarcoma. (Book p129)

questions.q: The most common benign bone tumor is:
questions.exp: Osteochondroma/exostosis is the m/c benign bone tumor. (Book p129)

questions.q: Most common site of osteochondroma:
questions.exp: m/c site: distal femur. (Book p129)

questions.q: Osteochondroma typically presents as:
questions.exp: Presents as a mass around the joint; sessile or pedunculated. (Book p129)

questions.q: Osteochondroma is sessile or pedunculated and is a developmental malformation of the:
questions.exp: Developmental malformation of growth plate - aberrant development. (Book p129)

questions.q: Direction of growth of osteochondroma:
opts: Epiphysis to metaphysis - away from the joint
Metaphysis to epiphysis - towards the joint
Along the long axis towards diaphysis
questions.exp: Follows normal direction of growth: epiphysis to metaphysis, away from the joint. (Book p129)

questions.q: Osteochondroma stops growing after skeletal maturity and is therefore:
questions.exp: Stops growing after skeletal maturity - not a true tumor. (Book p129)

questions.q: Clinically, osteochondroma is usually:
opts: Asymptomatic and grows with the skeleton
Present at birth as a large mass
questions.exp: Asymptomatic; grows with the skeleton and stops after skeletal maturity. (Book p129)

questions.q: Most common cause of pain in osteochondroma:
questions.exp: Pain causes: bursitis (m/c cause), nerve compression, fracture. (Book p129)

questions.q: Besides bursitis, other causes of pain in osteochondroma include:
questions.exp: Pain: bursitis (m/c), nerve compression, fracture. (Book p129)

questions.q: Osteochondroma undergoes malignant transformation into:
questions.exp: Malignant transformation → chondrosarcoma. (Book p129)

questions.q: MRI sign of malignant transformation in osteochondroma:
questions.exp: Signs: cap >2 cm on MRI; heavy calcification of cap on X-ray; persistence of growth after skeletal maturity. (Book p129)

questions.q: X-ray sign of malignant transformation in osteochondroma:
questions.exp: Heavy calcification of cap on X-ray; also persistence of growth after skeletal maturity. (Book p129)

questions.q: In osteochondroma, the lesion on palpation versus X-ray is:
opts: Large to feel but small on X-ray
Small to feel but large on X-ray
questions.exp: Large to feel but small on X-ray. (Book p130)

questions.q: The cartilaginous cap of osteochondroma cannot be visualized on X-ray because:
questions.exp: Cartilaginous cap (<2 cm) cannot be visualized on X-ray. (Book p130)

questions.q: CT of osteochondroma shows:
opts: Architecture of the lesion matches normal bone
questions.exp: CT: architecture of the lesion matches normal bone. (Book p130)

questions.q: Treatment of osteochondroma:
questions.exp: Treatment: extraperiosteal excision after skeletal maturity. (Book p130)

questions.q: Inheritance of hereditary multiple exostosis (diaphyseal aclasis):
questions.exp: Autosomal dominant inheritance. (Book p130)

questions.q: Gene mutation in hereditary multiple exostosis:
questions.exp: EXT 1, 2 gene mutation. (Book p130)

questions.q: In hereditary multiple exostosis, chondrosarcomatous change occurs in:
questions.exp: 5% cases → chondrosarcoma. (Book p130)

questions.q: Most common bone tumor of the small bones of hands and feet:
questions.exp: Enchondroma is the m/c bone tumor in small bones of hands and feet. (Book p130)

questions.q: Location of enchondroma:
questions.exp: Location: metaphyseal. (Book p130)

questions.q: Treatment of enchondroma:
questions.exp: Rx: extended curettage + bone graft. (Book p130)

questions.q: Ollier's syndrome consists of:
questions.exp: Ollier's syndrome: multiple enchondromas; very rare. (Book p130)

questions.q: Premalignant potential of Ollier's syndrome:
questions.exp: 30% cases of Ollier's are premalignant. (Book p130)

questions.q: Maffucci's syndrome is multiple enchondromas plus:
questions.exp: Maffucci's: multiple enchondromas + cavernous hemangiomas, lymphangiomas. (Book p130)

questions.q: Most common tumor of the hand:
questions.exp: m/c tumor of the hand: squamous cell carcinoma. (Book p130)

questions.q: Differential diagnosis for enchondroma in fingers (variant of TB involving fingers):
questions.exp: D/D for enchondroma: spina ventosa/TB dactylitis - variant of TB involving fingers. (Book p130)

questions.q: Chondroblastoma is also known as:
questions.exp: Chondroblastoma AKA Codman's tumor. (Book p131)

questions.q: Chondroblastoma is an___ lesion.
questions.exp: Chondroblastoma: epiphyseal lesion. (Book p131)

questions.q: Chondroblastoma occurs at what age?
questions.exp: m/c in children; 10-25 yrs (before skeletal maturity). (Book p131)

questions.q: X-ray of chondroblastoma shows:
questions.exp: X-ray: punctate/stippled calcification. (Book p131)

questions.q: Biopsy of chondroblastoma shows:
questions.exp: Biopsy: chicken wire calcifications. (Book p131)

questions.q: Treatment of chondroblastoma:
opts: Excision curettage with autologous bone graft
questions.exp: Treatment: excision curettage with autologous bone graft. (Book p131)

questions.q: Most common true benign bone tumor:
questions.exp: Osteoid osteoma is the m/c true benign tumor. (Book p131)

questions.q: Osteoid osteoma occurs in ___ located in the ___.
questions.exp: Children and adolescents; location: diaphysis. (Book p131)

questions.q: Most common site of osteoid osteoma:
questions.exp: m/c site: femur. (Book p131)

questions.q: Osteoid osteoma is which type of lesion?
questions.exp: Eccentric/cortical lesion. (Book p131)

questions.q: Pain in osteoid osteoma is produced by the:
questions.exp: Central nidus → produces prostaglandins → pain. (Book p131)

questions.q: Characteristic pain of osteoid osteoma:
opts: Night pain that responds to aspirin
questions.exp: Night pain that responds to aspirin; swelling in thigh or leg. (Book p131)

questions.q: X-ray of osteoid osteoma shows:
opts: Central lucent nidus with dense sclerosis around
questions.exp: X-ray: central lucent nidus with dense sclerosis around. (Book p131)

questions.q: Treatment of osteoid osteoma includes:
opts: NSAIDs, radiofrequency ablation, excision curettage, MR-guided focused ultrasound
questions.exp: Rx: NSAIDs (pain relief), radiofrequency ablation, excision curettage, MR-guided focused ultrasound destruction. (Book p131)

questions.q: Central nidus of osteoblastoma measures:
questions.exp: Osteoblastoma: central nidus >2 cm (vs osteoid osteoma). (Book p131)

questions.q: Osteoblastoma occurs in the:
questions.exp: Osteoblastoma occurs in spine. (Book p131)

questions.q: Response of osteoblastoma to aspirin:
questions.exp: Osteoblastoma may not respond to aspirin. (Book p131)

questions.q: Risk of malignant transformation of osteoblastoma is into:
questions.exp: Risk of malignant transformation → osteosarcoma. (Book p131)

questions.q: Treatment of osteoblastoma:
questions.exp: Treatment: surgical excision. (Book p131)

questions.q: Giant cell tumor is also known as:
questions.exp: GCT/osteoclastoma. (Book p132)

questions.q: Nature of giant cell tumor:
questions.exp: GCT is locally aggressive. (Book p132)

questions.q: Location of giant cell tumor:
questions.exp: Location: epiphysio-metaphyseal. (Book p132)

questions.q: Sex predilection of giant cell tumor:
questions.exp: Females > males. (Book p132)

questions.q: Age of giant cell tumor:
questions.exp: Age: 20-40 years (after skeletal maturity). (Book p132)

questions.q: Most common site of giant cell tumor:
questions.exp: Site: distal end of femur (m/c), proximal tibia - around the knee. (Book p132)

questions.q: Classical site of GCT and the m/c tumor occurring at the distal end of radius:
questions.exp: Distal end of radius (classical); m/c tumor of distal radius: osteoclastoma. (Book p132)

questions.q: Eggshell crackling in GCT occurs because:
questions.exp: Eggshell crackling: thin cortex breaks on palpation. (Book p132)

questions.q: X-ray of GCT shows soap bubble appearance due to:
questions.exp: Soap bubble appearance: leftover bony trabeculae after destruction. (Book p132)

questions.q: Biopsy of GCT shows:
opts: Multinucleated osteoclast-like giant cells surrounded by mononuclear tumor cells
Small round blue cells with rosettes
questions.exp: Biopsy: multinucleated osteoclast-like giant cells surrounded by mononuclear cells (tumor cells). (Book p132)

questions.q: Tumor cells of GCT produce increased:
questions.exp: Tumor cells → increased RANK ligand production. (Book p132)

questions.q: Treatment of GCT:
opts: Extended curettage with liquid nitrogen, phenol or bone cement
questions.exp: Extended curettage with liquid nitrogen, phenol or bone cement - to destroy residual cells. (Book p132)

questions.q: Extended curettage in GCT is followed by:
questions.exp: Followed by autologous bone graft. (Book p132)

questions.q: All are 'E' features of the GCT mnemonic except:
questions.exp: Mnemonic E: Epiphyseal location, after Epiphyseal fusion, Eccentric, Expansile, Eggshell crackling, Extended curettage. (Book p132)

questions.q: Most common tumor rich in giant cells:
questions.exp: Giant-cell-rich tumors: non-ossifying fibroma (m/c). (Book p132)

questions.q: Tumor with closest resemblance to GCT:
questions.exp: Aneurysmal bone cyst - closest resemblance to GCT. (Book p132)

questions.q: All of the following are giant-cell-rich tumors except:
questions.exp: Giant-cell-rich: NOF, ABC, chondromyxoid fibroma, chondroblastoma, fibrous dysplasia, SBC, brown tumor, telangiectatic osteosarcoma. (Book p132)

questions.q: Risk of malignant transformation in GCT is seen in:
questions.exp: Note: <5% cases - risk of malignant transformation. (Book p133)

questions.q: GCT transforms malignantly into:
opts: 2° osteosarcoma, fibrosarcoma, malignant fibrous histiocytoma (pleomorphic sarcoma)
questions.exp: Malignant transformation: 2° osteosarcoma, fibrosarcoma, MFH (pleomorphic sarcoma). (Book p133)

questions.q: Of the malignantly transformed GCTs, metastasis to lungs occurs in:
questions.exp: Transformed GCT: 3% metastasise to lungs. (Book p133)

questions.q: Local recurrence rate of GCT:
questions.exp: 30% cases: local recurrence. (Book p133)

questions.q: Bone hemangioma occurs in the:
questions.exp: Hemangioma occurs in elderly population. (Book p133)

questions.q: Nature of bone hemangioma:
questions.exp: Benign, asymptomatic vascular bone tumor. (Book p133)

questions.q: Site order of bone hemangioma:
questions.exp: Site: spine > skull > pelvis. (Book p133)

questions.q: Vertical striations on X-ray in vertebral hemangioma give rise to:
questions.exp: X-ray: vertical striations - jail bar/jail house appearance; corduroy appearance. (Book p133)

questions.q: Axial CT sign of bone hemangioma:
questions.exp: CT scan: polka dot sign (axial view). (Book p133)

questions.q: Treatment of bone hemangioma:
questions.exp: Treatment: conservative, radiotherapy, vertebroplasty. (Book p133)

questions.q: Vertebroplasty involves:
questions.exp: Vertebroplasty = injecting bone cement. (Book p133)

questions.q: Chondrosarcoma arises from the ___ in the age group of ___ .
questions.exp: Location: metaphysis; age: 40-50 yrs. (Book p133)

questions.q: Site of chondrosarcoma:
questions.exp: Site: pelvis, proximal femur (calcified tumor). (Book p133)

questions.q: Paraneoplastic syndrome associated with chondrosarcoma:
questions.exp: A/w paraneoplastic syndrome: hyperglycemia. (Book p133)

questions.q: X-ray of chondrosarcoma shows:
questions.exp: X-ray: endosteal scalloping and punctate calcification. (Book p133)

questions.q: Most common bone tumor seen in children:
questions.exp: Osteosarcoma is the m/c bone tumor seen in children. (Book p134)

questions.q: Bimodal presentation of osteosarcoma means:
opts: Children and elderly have equal peaks without cause
questions.exp: Bimodal: 1st decade 1° osteosarcoma; older population 2° osteosarcoma (Paget's/radiation). (Book p134)

questions.q: Which of the following is more common?
questions.exp: 1° osteosarcoma > 2° osteosarcoma. (Book p134)

questions.q: Radiation-induced osteosarcoma usually occurs after:
questions.exp: Radiation-induced osteosarcoma usually occurs 10 yrs after exposure. (Book p134)

questions.q: Location of osteosarcoma:
questions.exp: Location: metaphysis; distal end of femur. (Book p134)

questions.q: The most radio-resistant tumor is:
questions.exp: Osteosarcoma is the most radio-resistant tumor. (Book p134)

questions.q: Most common radiation-induced bone tumor:
questions.exp: Osteosarcoma is the m/c radiation-induced bone tumor. (Book p134)

questions.q: Osteosarcoma is a bone forming tumor; it forms:
questions.exp: Bone forming tumor: forms abnormal osteoid and matrix. (Book p134)

questions.q: 15% of osteosarcoma cases have micrometastasis to lungs at presentation, which can lead to:
questions.exp: 15% cases: micrometastasis to lungs during presentation → pneumothorax. (Book p134)

questions.q: Codman's triangle in osteosarcoma represents:
questions.exp: X-ray periosteal reaction: Codman's triangle - elevated periosteum. (Book p134)

questions.q: Sunburst appearance of osteosarcoma is due to:
questions.exp: Sunburst appearance: calcified Sharpey's fibres. (Book p134)

questions.q: Most common type of osteosarcoma:
questions.exp: Types: classical/intramedullary (m/c), periosteal, parosteal, telangiectatic. (Book p134)

questions.q: All of the following are types of osteosarcoma except:
questions.exp: Types: classical/intramedullary, periosteal, parosteal, telangiectatic. (Book p134)

questions.q: Treatment sequence of osteosarcoma:
opts: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy → surgery/limb ablation → adjuvant chemotherapy
questions.exp: Neoadjuvant chemo (prior to surgery) → surgery/limb ablation → adjuvant chemo (post surgery). (Book p134)

questions.q: Chemotherapeutic agents used in osteosarcoma (TID protocol) include:
opts: Actinomycin, cyclophosphamide, bleomycin, high-dose methotrexate, doxorubicin, vincristine
questions.exp: TID protocol: actinomycin, cyclophosphamide, bleomycin, high-dose methotrexate, doxorubicin, vincristine. (Book p135)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT part of the TID protocol?
questions.exp: TID protocol: actinomycin, cyclophosphamide, bleomycin, high-dose methotrexate, doxorubicin, vincristine. (Book p135)

questions.q: Most common tumor in the 1st decade of life:
questions.exp: Ewing sarcoma is the m/c tumor in the 1st decade of life. (Book p135)

questions.q: Occurrence of Ewing sarcoma is most common in:
questions.exp: Occurrence: m/c in the 2nd decade (5-20 yrs). (Book p135)

questions.q: Location of Ewing sarcoma:
questions.exp: Location: diaphysis of femur (mid-thigh swelling). (Book p135)

questions.q: Nature of Ewing sarcoma:
questions.exp: Males > females; high grade sarcoma. (Book p135)

questions.q: All of the following are poor prognostic features of Ewing sarcoma except:
questions.exp: Poor prognosis: metastasis, male, fever/anemia, ↑ESR, age >14 yrs, leukocytosis, chemoresistance, relapse, size of lesion. (Book p135)

questions.q: Poor prognostic age cut-off in Ewing sarcoma:
questions.exp: Age >14 yrs is a poor prognostic feature. (Book p135)

questions.q: Relapse and chemoresistance in Ewing sarcoma are:
questions.exp: Chemoresistance and relapse are poor prognostic features. (Book p135)

questions.q: Ewing sarcoma clinically presents like:
questions.exp: Presents like infection: mid-thigh/leg swelling, signs of inflammation, incidental h/o trauma. (Book p135)

questions.q: X-ray of Ewing sarcoma shows:
questions.exp: X-ray: onion peel/lamellated appearance. (Book p135)

questions.q: Best investigation for Ewing sarcoma:
questions.exp: Biopsy is the best investigation. (Book p135)

questions.q: Histopathology of Ewing sarcoma shows:
opts: Small, round blue cells with pseudo-rosettes
questions.exp: Biopsy: small, round blue cells with pseudo-rosettes. (Book p135)

questions.q: PAS staining in Ewing sarcoma:
questions.exp: PAS +ve and diastase digestible. (Book p135)

questions.q: Specific immunohistochemistry marker of Ewing sarcoma:
questions.exp: MIC-2 (CD99) on immunohistochemistry - specific marker. (Book p135)

questions.q: Most common karyotype translocation in Ewing sarcoma:
questions.exp: Karyotyping: t(11;22) m/c; other translocations t(21;22), t(7;22), trisomy 18, trisomy 12. (Book p135)

questions.q: Ewing sarcoma is radiosensitive, yet radiotherapy is not preferred because:
questions.exp: Radiosensitive, but radiotherapy not preferred d/t increased chance of recurrence. (Book p135)

questions.q: Current trend of treatment in Ewing sarcoma:
questions.exp: Current trend: chemotherapy + limb salvage/resection + adjuvant radiation. (Book p135)

questions.q: Primitive neuroectodermal tumors with small blue round cells on HPE include:
questions.exp: PNETs with small blue round cells on HPE: neuroblastoma, retinoblastoma, medulloblastoma. (Book p135)

questions.q: Chordoma originates from:
questions.exp: Origin: physaliferous cells of primitive notochord. (Book p136)

questions.q: Most common locations of chordoma:
questions.exp: m/c location: sacrum, base of skull, vertebrae; occurs in elderly. (Book p136)

questions.q: Adamantinoma is a:
opts: Low grade malignant epithelial tumor that grows into bone
questions.exp: Adamantinoma: low grade malignant epithelial tumor (that grows into bone). (Book p136)

questions.q: Most common bone for adamantinoma:
questions.exp: m/c bone: tibia (subcutaneous bone). (Book p136)

questions.q: Adamantinoma is diaphyseal; its X-ray shows:
questions.exp: Location: diaphysis; X-ray: diaphyseal soap bubble appearance. (Book p136)

questions.q: Synovial sarcoma:
opts: Does not arise from synovium - arises from capsule, bursae or tendon
questions.exp: Does not arise from synovium; arises from capsule, bursae or tendon. (Book p136)

questions.q: Cytogenetics of synovial sarcoma:
questions.exp: D/t t(x;18) → SYT : SSX fusion gene. (Book p136)

questions.q: Most common malignant bone tumor:
questions.exp: m/c malignant bone tumor: metastasis. (Book p136)

questions.q: Most common sources of bone metastasis in order:
questions.exp: Source: breast > prostate > lungs. (Book p136)

questions.q: Bone metastasis most commonly goes to:
questions.exp: m/c go to: lumbar vertebrae > thoracic vertebrae. (Book p136)

questions.q: Purely blastic secondaries are seen in:
questions.exp: Purely blastic: prostate, medulloblastoma, carcinoids. (Book p136)

questions.q: Purely lytic secondaries are seen in:
opts: Kidney (RCC) and follicular carcinoma of thyroid
questions.exp: Purely lytic: kidney (RCC), follicular carcinoma of thyroid. (Book p136)

questions.q: Mixed (or only lytic) secondaries are characteristic of:
questions.exp: Mixed: breast (or only lytic). (Book p136)

questions.q: Winking owl sign (destruction of pedicle on X-ray) is seen in:
questions.exp: Winking owl sign: destruction of pedicle. (Book p136)

questions.q: Bone-to-bone metastasis is seen in:
questions.exp: Bone to bone metastasis: Ewing sarcoma, osteosarcoma. (Book p136)

questions.q: Most common primary malignant bone tumor:
questions.exp: m/c primary malignant bone tumor: multiple myeloma > osteosarcoma; m/c non-haematological: osteosarcoma > chondrosarcoma. (Book p136)

questions.q: Most common benign bone tumor and most common true benign bone tumor respectively:
questions.exp: m/c benign bone tumor: osteochondroma; m/c true benign: osteoid osteoma. (Book p136)

units.title: Cartilaginous Lesions Intro
units.guide: Cartilage-forming tumors are chondrocyte predominant and announce themselves with popcorn, ring-and-arc (O-ring) calcification - the club of chondroma, osteochondroma and chondrosarcoma.

units.title: Osteochondroma: General Features
units.guide: Osteochondroma is the m/c benign bone tumor, m/c at the distal femur, a sessile or pedunculated mass that is aberrant growth-plate development. It grows epiphysis-to-metaphysis away from the joint, stops with skeletal maturity, and is not a true tumor.

units.title: Osteochondroma: Pain & Malignant Change
units.guide: Pain means bursitis first, then nerve compression or fracture. A cap over 2 cm on MRI, heavy cap calcification on X-ray, or growth persisting after skeletal maturity whispers chondrosarcoma.

units.title: Osteochondroma: Radiology & Rx
units.guide: Feel large, see small: the sub-2 cm cartilage cap hides from X-ray, while CT shows bone architecture matching normal. Cure is extraperiosteal excision after skeletal maturity.

units.title: Hereditary Multiple Exostosis
units.guide: Diaphyseal aclasis runs autosomal dominant through EXT 1,2 mutations, and 5% of the multiple lesions turn chondrosarcoma.

units.title: Enchondroma
units.guide: Enchondroma rules the small bones of hand and feet, sits metaphyseal, and gets extended curettage with bone graft.

units.title: Ollier's & Maffucci's
units.guide: Multiple enchondromas make Ollier's syndrome - very rare, 30% premalignant. When cavernous hemangiomas and lymphangiomas join in, it is Maffucci's.

units.title: Hand Tumor Note
units.guide: The hand's commonest tumor is squamous cell carcinoma, not a bone tumor. Enchondroma's great mimic in fingers is spina ventosa - TB dactylitis.

units.title: Chondroblastoma
units.guide: Codman's tumor claims the child's epiphysis at 10-25 years: stippled calcification on film, chicken-wire calcification on biopsy, cured by excision curettage with autologous graft.

units.title: Osteoid Osteoma
units.guide: The m/c true benign tumor: diaphyseal, cortical, femoral. Prostaglandins from the central nidus kindle night pain that aspirin quenches; a lucent nidus ringed by dense sclerosis seals the diagnosis - NSAIDs, RFA or excision.

units.title: Osteoblastoma
units.guide: Osteoblastoma is osteoid osteoma grown past 2 cm in the spine, may ignore aspirin, carries a whisper of osteosarcoma risk - excise it.

units.title: GCT: General Features
units.guide: Osteoclastoma: locally aggressive, epiphysio-metaphyseal, female-predominant, 20-40 years after skeletal maturity. Distal femur round the knee is the favourite seat, distal radius the classical one.

units.title: GCT: Clinical, Biopsy & Rx
units.guide: Eggshell crackling, a soap bubble of leftover trabeculae, giant cells around RANK-spewing mononuclear tumor cells. Extended curettage with liquid nitrogen, phenol or cement, then autograft - remember the six E's.

units.title: GCT Variants & Malignant Change
units.guide: Giant-cell-rich company: NOF most common, ABC closest in resemblance. Under 5% turn malignant (3% of those fly to the lungs), but 30% come back locally.

units.title: Hemangioma
units.guide: The elderly spine's quiet vascular blotch: jail bars (corduroy) on X-ray, polka dots on axial CT, spine > skull > pelvis. Treat conservatively, by radiotherapy or vertebroplasty - bone cement.

units.title: Chondrosarcoma
units.guide: Chondrosarcoma: 40-50 years, metaphyseal, in the pelvis and proximal femur as a calcified tumor with hyperglycemia as paraneoplasia. Endosteal scalloping and punctate calcification on film.

units.title: Osteosarcoma: General Features
units.guide: Children's commonest bone cancer: bimodal (1st decade 1°, older 2° via Paget/radiation), metaphyseal distal femur, radio-resistant, osteoid-forming. 15% already harbour lung micrometastases that can pop a pneumothorax.

units.title: Osteosarcoma: X-ray & Types
units.guide: Elevated periosteum draws Codman's triangle; calcified Sharpey's fibres burst into a sunburst. Classical intramedullary is the commonest of the four types.

units.title: Osteosarcoma: Rx & TID Chemo
units.guide: Map: neoadjuvant chemo, surgery/limb ablation, adjuvant chemo. Drugs - the TID protocol: actinomycin, cyclophosphamide, bleomycin, high-dose methotrexate, doxorubicin, vincristine.

units.title: Ewing: General & Prognosis
units.guide: Ewing owns the 1st decade, peaks in the 2nd (5-20 yrs) as a high-grade diaphyseal femur mass in boys. Metastasis, male sex, fever, anemia, raised ESR, age over 14, leukocytosis, chemoresistance and relapse all darken the outlook.

units.title: Ewing: Clinical, X-ray & Biopsy
units.guide: It masquerades as infection with an onion-peel film; biopsy - the best test - shows small round blue cells in pseudo-rosettes, PAS-positive and diastase digestible, MIC-2 (CD99) positive, carrying t(11;22).

units.title: Ewing: Rx & PNET Note
units.guide: Radiosensitive yet radiotherapy is shunned for fear of recurrence; today it is chemotherapy with limb salvage and adjuvant radiation. Neuroblastoma, retinoblastoma and medulloblastoma share the small-blue-round-cell club.

units.title: Chordoma, Adamantinoma & Synovial
units.guide: Chordoma rises from notochord rests in the elderly sacrum; adamantinoma, a low-grade epithelial malignancy, soap-bubbles the tibial diaphysis; synovial sarcoma ignores synovium, born of capsule, bursae or tendon with t(x;18) SYT:SSX.

units.title: Metastasis & Key Summary
units.guide: Metastasis is the commonest malignant bone tumor - breast, prostate, lung riding to the lumbar spine. Prostate blastic, kidney and follicular thyroid lytic, breast mixed; the winking owl is a eaten pedicle. Myeloma heads the malignant list, osteochondroma the benign, osteoid osteoma the true-benign.
